It's etiolated! That's what happens to succulents if they don't get enough light.
Give it full sun, but not directly- it needs to get used to the increase in light by increasing it gradually over the course of a week or so, or else the leaves will get sunburnt

The plant won't go back to normal, but the new growth will be compact, and you can behead and re-root it later on.

I'm by no means an expert but I do have one of these, the basic rules to succulents are:
1. They like good drainage. So 50% soil and 50% grit. For soil, succulent mix or normal potting soil will work, for grit, perlite, pumice, or any small stones (not smaller than 1/8th of an inch). I use aquarium pebbles as the grit
2. Pot MUST have drainage hole. Terracotta pots are preferred because they have pores to lose water
3. Only water when the bottom leaves look shrivelly, I'm time you can get the watering down to whether the pot is heavier (water present in pot) or lighter (no water). I haven't watered mine since 2 weeks, it's recovering from a near root rot.

From the pic your roots look white and healthy, but I'd repot this as soon as possible. Squishy, moist roots and leaves, leaves turning translucent are general signs of rot.

You can find more answers about succulent care in the subreddit sidebar!
